title: Provide deterministic provider-free reference adapters for target use-case tests

requirements.invariant: Target use-case tests have deterministic in-memory and failure reference adapters in a target-only module while the released Firebase application remains unchanged and the target application contains no Firebase data adapter.
A validated synthetic test context supplies fixed environment, Principal, Account, clock, identifiers and revisions without process-global time, randomness, Firebase, Supabase or PowerSync modules.

Finite immutable scripts drive the shared operation-query and sync-health ports through local receipt, authoritative result, retry, rejection, required-update, maintenance and Account-context outcomes with explicit exhaustion and no external state.

The in-memory reference adapters conform to the same backend-neutral Ledger ports that later local and cloud target adapters must satisfy; Firebase export fixtures remain migration evidence and never become application adapters.

The separate test-support module depends inward only on LedgerTargetCore, is linked by neither application, and exposes only Ledger and standard Swift types with no provider, database, file or transport import.

items: DeterministicTargetTestContext binds one validated non-production TargetEnvironmentManifest, synthetic PrincipalID, synthetic AccountID, bounded ScenarioID, stable seed and integer epoch-millisecond base time before any fixture or adapter exists.

DeterministicTargetValueSource derives domain-separated fixed timestamps, IDs and monotonic revisions by stable key/index and exposes finite schedules with explicit exhaustion; it never reads a process clock, UUID generator, randomness, filesystem, network or mutable global.

ScriptedOperationQueryAdapter and ScriptedSyncHealthAdapter conform to OperationQuerying and SyncHealthProviding and expose finite immutable Account-scoped success/failure scripts with stable safe errors and no provider-shaped values.
DeterministicTargetScenario validates complete context and scripts, normalizes equivalent input order, emits bounded canonical evidence and reconstructs only through the same validation boundary.

postgresSchema.notApplicable: This reference test-support slice creates no Postgres table, relationship, constraint, index, view or migration.

serverHandlers.notApplicable: No authoritative command handler, transaction, lock or server-side idempotency implementation runs; scripts only return already-typed reference outcomes.

dataApiGrants.notApplicable: No schema, relation, view or function is exposed through the Supabase Data API.

rlsPolicies.notApplicable: There are no server rows or API roles. Account isolation is structural fixture validation, not a substitute for later RLS tests.

syncStreams.notApplicable: Scripted SyncHealthSnapshot values exercise the port contract without defining or starting a PowerSync Stream, bucket, local table or upload queue.

items: A scenario encodes to bounded canonical bytes and reconstructs offline with exactly the same context, deterministic value schedules and adapter outcomes; equivalent input order produces identical evidence.

Production/unsafe environment binding, nonfixture identity, cross-Account access, duplicate or conflicting keys, invalid or nonmonotonic schedules, script exhaustion, noncanonical bytes, digest tamper and oversized evidence fail atomically with stable safe codes.

Reference adapters distinguish cached/local observations from queued and authoritative outcomes, preserve online-versus-synchronized truth, and can model retry, permanent rejection, required update, maintenance and Account switch without network or database state.

storageMedia.notApplicable: No attachment metadata, bytes, path, URL, upload script or retention behavior exists; media fault adapters require their own gated slice.

appMcp.notApplicable: This slice supplies shared reference port adapters only. It does not wire concrete app or MCP entry points, claim transport parity, or replace current Swift/MCP helper surfaces.

migrationReconciliation.notApplicable: No Firebase export fixture, source transform, target load or production-derived record is used. Domain-specific and migration fixture catalogs remain later slices.

observabilityRunbooks.notApplicable: The module emits no telemetry, metric, alert or runbook action; stable test refusal codes remain local test values only.

items: The module and self-tests are additive target-only Swift package targets that depend only on LedgerTargetCore, are absent from both application project graphs, contact no hosted service and change no Firebase source or behavior.

The module is test authority only: it cannot activate a feature, choose a provider, approve a product rule, prove local database or physical-device fidelity, deploy, migrate, release or authorize cutover.
TEST-6A6B0926E2EE and FILE-F29942C1A7F4 remain target_mapped until domain-specific semantic fixtures and concrete app/MCP/local/cloud adapter suites cover their broader outcomes.

verification.expected: Validated synthetic context and deterministic value schedules are exact and stable, and the reference operation-query/sync-health adapters emit the configured typed outcomes through the shared LedgerTargetCore ports.

Canonical scenario evidence reconstructs offline after restart and emits the identical fixed clock, IDs, revisions, operation snapshots, health snapshots and stable failures independent of input ordering.

Production or unsafe binding, credential/provider material, nonfixture or cross-Account identity, duplicate/conflicting/nonmonotonic scripts, exhaustion, noncanonical bytes, digest tamper and oversized evidence fail with stable safe codes and no partial advancement.

verification.owner: pull-request CI Isolated target environment job
verification.expected: The exact implementation commit passes conversion traceability, package graph/provider/source-contamination guards, the complete target package suite, both target builds and clean artifacts while neither application links the test-support module.

notes: Decision-independent Phase 1 technical-control foundation only. The implementation and first three obligations pass locally; exact-commit hosted CI remains before verification. It stops before domain-specific product fixtures, current app/MCP helper replacement, local database or PowerSync behavior, provider SDKs, hosted staging, migration fixtures, physical offline claims, A-003/A-004/A-007/A-015/A-016, open product decisions, deployment, production access or cutover authority.
